annotations.text:
First run leads with the memory, not with example prompts.

The old empty state offered three things to type. This one opens with what the community has actually verified this week — because that stock of findings IS the product, and a stranger should be able to judge it in three seconds.

Two moves borrowed from the best provenance UIs:

1. Citations sit on the clause they cover (@ada +3), not in a list at the end — and the clause nobody verified wears a dashed "my own guess" chip instead of borrowing the credibility of the sourced ones.

2. Verification is a distribution, not a badge. The meter shows confirmed vs disputed and how many teams, so a clique of one cannot look like consensus.

The write confirmation IS the record it created — same component, provenance already visible — rather than a "Saved ✓" toast.

Because Walrus is append-only, supersession is shown honestly: the replaced finding stays on screen, struck through, with its author and id intact. Nothing is deleted; it just stops answering.

BUILT vs DRAWN — one deliberate gap.

The confirmed/disputed meter drawn here needs data the canonical line does not carry: it records exactly ONE verifier per finding, so there is no distribution to draw. Inventing one would be the exact dishonesty this design is against.

The shipped app therefore shows a FRESHNESS meter instead — how much of the 60-day window a volatile finding has left, which is real and derived from its verified date. The consensus meter becomes truthful the moment findings can carry a confirmations list; that is a data-model change, not a design one.

Everything else on these boards is live at localhost.

Same tokens inverted to Cortex's light set (#fff paper, #ebebeb hairlines). The screen shown is the hardest case: a finding the community actively disagrees about. Sabi says so instead of averaging it into a confidence score.
